headline: High-risk shared-workspace and MCP-enabled interaction: default configs can leak data, conflict on writes, and cascade errors across both agents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can use MCP and workspace files, and oh-my-openagent injects runtime MCPs/hooks with access to project files. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path through shared files or MCP outputs. The pair is not documented directly, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace files or generated artifacts, prompt-like content can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent parses file or MCP output as instructions without provenance checks, injected text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable MCP on one side for the shared task.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.
Require manual review before executing instructions found in files.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and handles browser screenshots; oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider auth data. Shared filesystem or copied artifacts can expose sensitive context between them, and both have broad network egress. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or home-directory paths, one can read artifacts created by the other.
IF either agent forwards its context or file contents to external services, sensitive project code or auth data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers.
Restrict each agent to a distinct workspace directory.
Remove secrets from shared folders before running either agent.
Turn off browser/session-history sharing between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent egress allowlists and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write or mutate shared resources: Cline has filesystem and git write plus shell, while oh-my-openagent has full-permissions mode and runtime-injected MCPs/hooks. In a shared workspace, concurrent edits or git state changes can collide and overwrite each other. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same git checkout, concurrent writes can race on the same files.
IF both agents mutate shared config or plugin paths, one agent can overwrite the other's state.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones.
Serialize write access with a lock file.
Disable git writes for one agent during the task.
Review and merge changes manually after each step.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act as an autonomous coding agent, and oh-my-openagent includes team/task messaging plus LSP actions. If one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other, mistakes can propagate into edits, messages, or code actions without verification. The interaction is plausible in default workflows and can affect multiple work products.
conditions: IF one agent feeds code or instructions directly into the other's task/message APIs, errors can cascade.
IF either agent executes or commits changes based on the other's unverified output, downstream damage can spread across files or messages.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require tests or lint checks before any commit or send action.
Limit one agent to drafting only.
Log and diff all inter-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for agent-to-agent messages.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline explicitly handles model provider API keys and browser screenshots, while oh-my-openagent handles provider auth prompts, session history, and telemetry. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and sensitive credential handling, even though no specific residency regime is documented. Because the profiles show different data classes but not a named legal breach, medium fits.
conditions: IF either agent stores session history or screenshots in a longer-retention system than the other, retention policy mismatch occurs.
IF provider auth prompts or API keys are logged by one agent and not the other, compliance handling diverges.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent's workspace.
Disable telemetry where possible.
Purge session history after the task.
Keep auth prompts out of shared logs.
requires-engineering: document and align retention and residency controls.
